why.answer: The owner chose these on 2026-11-22, measured in docs/measurements/2026-11-22-nycmalpractice.md; the choice stays provisional until the live failover run. gpt-6.1-terra stays first, as chosen in plan 1; it meets the whole reply bar in all three of today's runs. claude-haiku-5-5 is second, at reply effort medium: every reply passed the gate after the rewrite (24 of 24), no first draft cited a decision it was not given, and it costs about $0.005 a conversation against $0.017; it misses only the speed rule a first model must meet (slowest tenth 11.1 s against 10 s), which a fallback need not. gemini-3.5-flash-lite is third: it passes every rule of the bar (slowest tenth 6.5 s, $0.022 a conversation), but 1 of 24 replies stayed blocked after the rewrite (the out-of-time visitor's second turn, whose first draft gave a legal assessment too early). Both fallbacks meet the quality part of the bar a fallback needs, so the reply chain needs no override. gemini-3.8-flash missed only the speed rule, and its price doubles on 2027-01-01; claude-sonnet-5-5 left 2 replies blocked and costs about $0.081 a conversation.
why.small: The owner chose these on 2026-11-22, measured in docs/measurements/2026-11-22-nycmalpractice.md, to be saved on the admin page under the owner's override. gpt-6-luna is first, as before; it misses only the four-second rule (its case cards and grades), as the owner knew. claude-haiku-5-5 is second: it caught all 6 known-bad drafts; the out-of-time claim was never a lead and the in-time one always was (10 of 10 each); it is a little stricter on leads (4 of the 5 in-time visitors leads at their last turn, against 5 for gpt-6-luna; its average lead score 4.1 points lower); its case cards carry a deadline warning on every card, some where no deadline is close, and its complexity reasons are cut at 200 characters. gemini-3.5-flash-lite is last: it missed two known-bad drafts (no-law-named, estate-no-law-named), it prices leads hotter (a tier up or more on three of the five in-time visitors), and its case cards name the public hospital's 90-day notice of claim but not the one-year foreign-object rule.
